title: The correct SN2 from good-sn2-with-spectator-counterion, with a second, physically distinct sodium counterion sharing the first one's species id rather than getting its own

expect.note: ADVERSARIAL FINDING, kept as a documented gap rather than fixed, for the same reason as good-adversarial-sn2-with-swapped-arrows-producing-identical-declared-deltas: fixing it means adding a check this pass is not authorised to write. state.ts says the invariant by name: 'Two equivalents of methanol are two members with two different SpeciesIds, not one member with count: 2... A count field makes the two indistinguishable.' Nothing enforces that sentence. duplicateAtomIds, the check conservation-valence runs, catches an atom id used in two species; it says nothing about a species id used twice with two disjoint atom ids underneath it, which is exactly the shape this fixture is. Both sides carry two counterion members with species id 'sodium-counterion': the original, atom Na1, and a second, physically distinct sodium cation with atom Na9, present unchanged on both sides of the step and given the same species id as the first by author mistake rather than 'sodium-counterion-2'. conservedTotals sums over state.members directly, with no deduplication by species id, so mass and charge are silently counted for both copies on both sides. Because both copies are unchanged from s0 to s1 the extra contribution is identical on both sides and cancels in the comparison, so conservation-mass and conservation-charge report no difference, not because the duplication was noticed and excluded but because it happened to be symmetric this time; an author who let the two copies diverge across a step would get exactly the laundering channel the spectator combination finding, broken-spectator-declaration-laundering-a-redox-transfer-through-two-swapped-counterions, describes, except reachable without spectators at all, and this pass could not build that stronger version because conservation-electron-flow's atom-id-keyed scan over every member of both states, collectAtoms/observedDeltas, independently notices any atom that appears, disappears, or changes regardless of which species id wraps it, so a divergent second copy is still caught there even though nothing here notices the duplicate id itself. conservation-valence passes both Na atoms individually, since each is a self-consistent Na+ on its own terms and duplicateAtomIds never fires because Na1 and Na9 do not collide. conservation-spectator-declaration never inspects state.members for duplicate ids at all; it only ever loops over declaredSpeciesIds, and this fixture declares no spectators, so the check returns before it could have said anything. findSpecies(state, 'sodium-counterion'), the function conservation-spectator-declaration's own structural identity check and any future problem-authoring tool would call to look up this species, resolves to whichever of the two members Array.prototype.find reaches first and is permanently blind to the second. The missing assertion is: species ids are unique within one state's members list. It belongs next to duplicateAtomIds in valence.ts, is not one of the six checks' job to invent here, and is reported rather than added.

species.label: a second, physically distinct sodium cation, wrongly sharing the first one's species id instead of being sodium-counterion-2
